title: the cave of Svayamprabha
hook: lost, thirsty, and following wet birds into the dark

segments.voice: Yesterday: the search parties. Three came home empty, and the south carries Rama's ring. Did you give someone a token of trust? Day five hundred ninety-six.

The southern party is having a terrible time. They've searched the Vindhya hills, forest after forest, cave after cave. Nothing. Now they're lost, hungry, and desperately thirsty. They've wandered into dry country with no stream in sight, and the month is running out. And then they see birds flying out of a hole in the hillside: cranes, geese, waterbirds, their wings wet. Where there are wet birds, there's water somewhere. So in they go.
screen: `LOST IN THE VINDHYA HILLS.` → `THIRSTY.` → `WET BIRDS FROM A HOLE.`

segments.voice: The cave is dark and overgrown with creepers. Valmiki calls it Rikshabila, the bear's hole. Hanuman goes first. The monkeys hold on to one another in the pitch black and go deeper and deeper, for a long way. And then light. They come out into a place that shouldn't exist underground: golden trees glowing like fire, palaces of gold and silver, lotus pools, and heaps of food, fruit and honey. They had to hold on to each other in the dark and keep going, with no idea what was at the end. In the middle of it all sits a woman ascetic, dressed in bark and black antelope skin, shining with her own light. Hanuman approaches with joined palms and asks: whose place is this? She tells them. It was built by Maya, the great architect of the demons, by his own powers. He lived here with Hema, a celestial dancer, until Indra killed him. Now it belongs to Hema. And I, she says, am Svayamprabha, daughter of Merusavarni. I keep it for my friend. Her name means shining by herself. Then comes what she does next. She doesn't question them or test them. Eat first, she says. Drink. Rest. Then tell me your story. Lost travelers, fed by an ascetic in a hidden golden city, and nothing asked of them first.
screen: `INTO THE BEAR'S HOLE.` · `HOLDING ON IN THE DARK.` · `A GOLDEN CITY BUILT BY MAYA.` · `EAT FIRST, THEN TALK.`

segments.voice: If there's water near you, take one slow sip. If not, just notice your mouth and throat. Breathe in, and remember the monkeys, parched, following wet wings into the dark. Breathe out, and let the sip, or the breath, be enough for now. Then rest your hands and sit like a guest who has been given what they need before anyone asked them a single question. The bell holds the time.
The cave of Svayamprabha. A dark hole, a golden city built by Maya, and a self-shining ascetic who feeds them first.
Your line: the cave of Svayamprabha. Today, when someone arrives tired, offer food or a drink before you ask them anything. Day five hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: Svayamprabha is remembered as one of the Ramayana's ascetic women, alongside Shabari; in many retellings her cave is a short, mysterious interlude before the search reaches the sea.

fork.setup: you're a monkey in the southern party, dying of thirst. birds with wet wings fly out of a dark hole. what do you do?
options: go into the dark, holding on to each other.
fork.reveal: they go in hand in hand, and find a golden city with food, water and Svayamprabha.

original.note: Sanskrit svayamprabhā: 'self-shining', from svayam (by oneself) + prabhā (light, radiance).

trapdoor: what you thought: the cave is a detour.
what it means: it's a place of rest and hospitality inside the hardest stretch of the search.
what a scholar hears: Kishkindha 50 names the cave Ṛkṣabila; Kishkindha 51 has Svayamprabha's account of Maya, Hema and her own father, Merusavarni.
